description: Whether an ordinary http/https page sees chrome.runtime and window.browser, which is decided entirely by whether some installed extension's externally_connectable manifest key matches the page: CanWebpageContextConnectExternally in extensions/renderer/native_extension_bindings_system.cc walks the renderer's extension set and returns true on the first match, and UpdateBindingsForContext installs the runtime accessor and the browser object from that answer alone. Conditioned on nothing. It is a fact about what the machine's owner installed, and nothing else in a profile predicts that: the same wallet extension is on Windows, macOS and Linux desktops alike, so keying this on the platform or the machine class would invent a correlation the population does not have. Presence-only by design -- the axis never names an extension id, because a fixed id is a cross-instance correlator that survives every other axis, and an inert component extension shipped to supply one would be worse than the surface it closes.
label: extensions

options.note: MEASURED, and the default state: a browser with no extension matching the page has no chrome.runtime there, so false is what fresh Chrome reports and what most real launches should. It is served as an explicit false rather than as an absent section, because absence would leave the host's own extension set to answer a question the persona is supposed to own. The folklore that a full Chrome always exposes chrome.runtime comes from the CryptoToken component extension, which shipped externally_connectable https://*/* in every Chrome and Chromium build until roughly Chrome 98 and has not existed since 2022. The 75/25 split is authored, not a survey: it states that the minority of real machines carry a wallet-shaped extension, and no public dataset gives the fraction.
options.source: own measurement, stock Google Chrome 153.0.8010.48 on a fresh --user-data-dir: Object.getOwnPropertyNames(chrome) is ['loadTimes','csi','app'] and typeof chrome.runtime is 'undefined' on https://example.com/ and on file:///; Apostate 152 matches it field for field under a composed Windows persona

options.note: AUTHORED PREVALENCE, MEASURED SHAPE. The observable was measured on stock Chrome with a MetaMask-shaped manifest: window.chrome gains 'runtime', window.browser appears carrying only 'runtime', the two are the same object, and the runtime object holds connect, sendMessage, the six enum objects and the id/dynamicId accessors reading undefined -- while file:// and about:blank stay bare, because the manifest matches http and https only. What is authored is the weight. Serving this state means reproducing it through the real binding path: sendMessage and connect to any id answer with message_service.cc's kReceivingEndDoesntExistError, which is the same answer a real browser gives for an id that is installed but not connectable, so no enumeration oracle is created.
options.source: MetaMask/metamask-extension app/manifest/v3/chrome.json externally_connectable {matches: ['http://*/*', 'https://*/*'], ids: ['*']}, tens of millions of installs; the same shape in AmbireTech/extension and ethereum/kohaku-extension; own measurement of that manifest loaded unpacked into a fresh stock Chrome 153 profile, which reproduced the field-for-field surface a Google-owned externally-connectable extension produces on its own origins
